headline: OpenAI launches GPT 5.6, enhancing AI capabilities with the new Sol/Terra/Luna models.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT 5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna, Codex becomes ChatGPT superapp
items.summary: OpenAI has released GPT 5.6, introducing the Sol, Terra, and Luna models. This release significantly enhances AI capabilities, integrating the Codex model into a broader ChatGPT superapp. The new models promise improved performance and efficiency, focusing on diverse applications across industries. This update aims to streamline AI integration into business processes, offering more robust and versatile AI tools to developers.
items.why_it_matters: This release highlights a major advancement in AI model capabilities, offering new opportunities for integrating sophisticated AI systems into applications.

items.title: Migrating a production AI agent to GPT-5.6: 2.2x faster, 27% cheaper
items.summary: A detailed exploration of upgrading a production AI agent to use the newly released GPT-5.6 model. The migration results in a 2.2x speed increase and a 27% reduction in operational costs, showcasing the efficiency and performance improvements of the latest AI model. The process involved testing and optimization to ensure seamless integration with existing systems.

items.title: shot-scraper 1.11

items.title: sqlite-utils 4.1.1
items.summary: The new version 4.1.1 of sqlite-utils addresses an edge case identified through Claude chat, providing critical fixes that enhance the tool’s reliability and performance. This update is essential for developers relying on sqlite-utils for managing SQLite databases.

items.title: Interval Certifications for Multilayered Perceptrons via Lattice Traversal
items.summary: This research presents a theoretical framework for addressing adversarial robustness in AI, specifically focusing on multilayered perceptrons. By reducing the problem to a lattice traversal, the study offers new insights into improving AI safety and robustness against adversarial attacks.

items.title: GATS: Graph-Augmented Tree Search with Layered World Models for Efficient Agent Planning
items.summary: This paper introduces GATS, a novel approach to agent planning that integrates graph-augmented tree search with layered world models. The method aims to reduce computational costs and improve efficiency in multi-step planning tasks, offering a significant advancement for developing intelligent agents.
